{"notes": "Visit 3 (left 5:30, about 4.5 min left). Open risk: the back arc is still not connected to the tail. It is dark only to about x=23, y=9.3. Two pale stubs sit at x~23.5-24.4 and the pale top tail starts around x=26, so a gap of roughly 1.5 units remains. Nothing visible from the sweep yet, and the facilitator pushes at the 10:00 mark. The bottom tail is dark all the way round to about (27.3, 10.4), but a small gap of under 1 unit remains to the pale tail's lower end (~27.3, 9.7). Everything hinges on the top join.

Sofia: Clear, repeated communication. She took Omar's geometry advice (wider, gentler sweep) and told Jack and Hana what she was doing. But the join she owns is still open with time short, so I can't credit it yet. I haven't seen her place pieces. Check whether the sweep lands.

Omar: Strongest evidence so far. At 4:30 he announced the belly landing and handed off to Jack. He gave Sofia a useful geometry fix and verified the handover. His claim that the bottom tail is dark matches the table. Good collaboration and real leadership. I don't know who placed which dominoes.

Hana: Responsive. She stayed clear of Sofia's work, said her tail would go dark once the sweep reaches it, and offered to check the join. Reasonable coordination, but passive and dependent on Sofia. Her tail is worth credit only if the join holds.

Jack: Still said nothing I heard. The bottom tail is now dark, and Omar named him for it, but I didn't see who built it. I'll avoid crediting him by assumption and ask him privately or at the review."}
